question: What do WIR, Sardex, LETS and liquidity-saving obligation clearing studies establish about mutual credit and multilateral clearing?

frame.exposure: mutual credit; multilateral netting of obligations

item.title: Complementary credit networks and macroeconomic stability: Switzerland’s Wirtschaftsring
item.container-title: Journal of Economic Behavior and Organization

findings.finding: WIR credit provides residual spending power that is counter-cyclical: individuals short of cash in a recession use more WIR credit; WIR money is negatively correlated with GDP in the short run, confirmed by empirical estimates.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: Thus, unlike the ordinary money, WIR money is negatively correlated with GDP in the short run. This implication is confirmed by empirical estimates.

findings.finding: Founded 1934; such credit networks play a stabilizing role that should be considered in monetary policy.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: Such credit networks play a stabilizing role that should be considered in monetary policy.

sources.population: the Swiss WIR credit network, founded 1934, time series against GDP
notFound: Sample length, coefficients and n are in the article body, subscription-only.

item.title: Liquidity-saving through obligation-clearing and mutual credit: an effective monetary innovation for SMEs in times of crisis
item.container-title: Journal of Risk and Financial Management

findings.finding: On real Sardex data, obligation-clearing alone reduces net internal debt of the obligation network by about 25 percent, and by about 50 percent when combined with mutual credit as a liquidity source.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: Real data from the Sardex mutual credit system show a reduction of net internal debt of the obligation network of approximately 25% when obligation-clearing is used by itself and of 50% when it is used together with mutual credit.

findings.finding: Clearing is recommended to extend to the tax authority as a node in the obligation network.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: The paper concludes by outlining recommendations for how even greater savings could be achieved by including the tax authority as another node in the obligation network.

sources.population: obligation network of the Sardex mutual credit system, Sardinia
notFound: Number of firms and obligations in the dataset are in the article body, which the publisher site did not serve.

item.title: Mathematical foundations for balancing the payment system in the trade credit market
item.container-title: Journal of Risk and Financial Management

findings.finding: Proves that the liquidity saved by obligation-clearing is maximum for a payment system with any number of liquidity sources, using graph theory, and defines a balanced payment subsystem that can be settled in full and removed.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: the main output of the paper is the proof—for the general formulation of a payment system with an arbitrary number of liquidity sources—that the amount of liquidity saved is maximum

sources.population: payment systems with arbitrary numbers of liquidity sources

item.title: Deepening the secondary market: integrating trade credit into market clearing with the Cycles Protocol

findings.finding: Trade credit is large: accounts payable of US non-financial firms are about three times bank credit and fifteen times commercial paper; trade credit balances are about 20 percent of GDP across advanced economies; supplier trade credit sustains up to 14 percent higher output and absorbs roughly 45 percent of output losses in modelled shocks.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: accounts payable on the balance sheets of non-financial US firms are roughly three times larger than bank credit and fifteen times larger than commercial paper

findings.finding: Slovenian national multilateral trade-credit clearing over 111 monthly cycles: 80,124 unique firms, 5,880,447 obligations, average monthly volume 269 million euro, average obligation 5,464 euro; the network shrank from about 24,000 firms (2016) to about 11,000 (2025) while average obligation rose from 4,217 to 7,320 euro.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: The dataset shows that the network shrank markedly during the observation period, from about 24,000 firms in 2016 to about 11,000 in 2025, while the average obligation size nearly doubled from €4,217 to €7,320.

findings.finding: Liquidity-provider firms hold 12.8 percent of submitted debt, yet removing them cuts cleared value 55.5 percent on average (range 31.8 to 71.2); direct liquidity-provider share of obligations 8.9 percent, adjusted contribution 37.9 percent, matching field estimates of 40 to 50 percent.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: LP firms represent approximately 12.8% of total submitted debt (std 2.7%), yet their exit causes a disproportionate collapse in clearing.

findings.finding: The Cycles Protocol: distributed multilateral clearing by double-entry accounting and atomic cycle execution that compresses balance sheets without novation, so counterparty risk is not redistributed; the Slovenian evidence is descriptive and shows no performance of a protocol implementation.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: It does not show the performance, security, or governance properties of any specific protocol implementation nor identify causal effects or welfare impacts.

sources.population: Slovenian national trade credit clearing, 111 monthly cycles May 2016 to March 2025, administrative records of the AJPES agency

item.title: Self-funded social impact investment: an interdisciplinary analysis of the Sardex mutual credit system

findings.finding: Sardex generates private funding endogenously within a bounded socio-economic context and is argued to be a form of self-funded social impact investment.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: It allows private funding to be endogenously generated within a geographically limited socio-economic context, rather than injected from exogenous sources, leading to a greater level of positive social impact.

sources.population: 29 semi-structured in-depth interviews of Sardex members

item.title: The alter-politics of complementary currencies: the case of Sardex

findings.finding: A market that mediates only the real economy and shuts out the financial economy can provide sustainability by supporting SMEs and a shield against financial crises, in the authors’ reading of Sardex.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: a market that mediates the (local) real economy only and shuts out the financial economy can provide economic sustainability by supporting SMEs, supply a shield against the adverse effects of financial crises

item.title: Local exchange and trading systems: a new source of work and credit for the poor and unemployed?

findings.finding: LETS were growing rapidly and a high proportion of national membership were poor and unemployed, but use was mainly by a disenfranchised middle class; wider inclusion needs changes in the operating environment and in the government approach to benefit claimants.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: although the poor and unemployed are capitalising on LETS to gain access to work and credit, it is utilised mainly by what can be called the ‘disenfranchised middle class’

sources.population: national survey of LETS and a membership survey of Manchester LETS
notFound: Survey n values are in the article body, not in the abstract.
